title: Serialize egress policy updates to prevent tenant resolver race
creator: Aarav Mehta
description: Several enterprise customers on Dedicated nodes experienced intermittent cross-tenant name resolution and short windows where tenant traffic resolved to previously-evicted hostnames after rapid peering handoffs and concurrent egress policy updates. This ticket implements a deterministic serialization layer for egress policy changes and resolver binding updates to eliminate races that can cause transient tenant isolation lapses.
observed_behavior: During scale-down/peering handoff scenarios, a subset of requests from Tenant A intermittently resolved via Tenant B's resolver binding for up to 10s. Symptoms observed: temporary connection failures, 502/504s surfaced to customers, and customer escalations citing hostname misresolution. Incidents correlate with bursts of policy updates plus concurrent SNAT/egress-binding churn.
expected_behavior: Egress policy updates and resolver binding changes should be applied atomically with per-tenant ordering guarantees such that in-flight requests never observe a mismatched resolver binding belonging to another tenant. No cross-tenant name resolution or transient hostname reassignment should occur.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision two tenants (T-A, T-B) on the same Dedicated region with VPC peering enabled.
2) Create a load pattern that causes frequent dedicated-node scale-down and node-eviction events.
3) Rapidly apply and rollback egress policy changes for T-A while simultaneously triggering peering route updates for T-B.
4) Observe DNS lookups and connection attempts from T-A during the window; capture resolver binding state and kernel SNAT table at high frequency.
5) Reproduce observed transient misresolution within ~5–15s of coordinated policy churn.
root_cause: Race between the async egress-policy reconciler and the resolver-binding reconciler. Both subsystems mutate shared in-memory binding tables and emit control-plane updates to dataplane agents without global serialization or version checks. Under concurrent updates, a stale resolver binding from a pre-eviction session could be re-applied to a tenant context while SNAT entries were being recycled, producing transient cross-tenant resolution.
mitigation_workaround: 1) Short-term: throttle concurrent policy updates per-tenant (configured at control plane) and increase tenant-specific reconciliation backoff to reduce churn. 2) Deploy temporary evasive guard in dataplane: validate resolver-owner before honoring cache entries and drop any mapping that doesn't match current tenant id. Applied as emergency patch to affected clusters.
permanent_fix_overview: Introduce a serialization queue for egress-policy and resolver-binding mutations keyed by tenant-id. Each mutation will carry a monotonic epoch and be applied in order; dataplane agents will accept bindings only if epoch is >= current committed epoch. Add strong invariants and checks to SNAT allocator to prevent reusing ephemeral ports until epoch advance completes. Update reconciliation logic to use compare-and-swap semantics for in-memory binding table updates.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Implement serialization queue and epoch propagation, ship to a single low-traffic Dedicated zone (canary) and run synthetic tenant churn tests with 10x policy update rate.
Phase 2 (Gradual): Expand to 25% of Dedicated capacity across two regions, monitor DNS misresolution rate and 5xx spike metrics for 48 hours.
Phase 3 (Full): Apply control-plane defaults for serialization and epoch checks across Dedicated clusters, then remove temporary throttles and guard code after 1 week of stable metrics.
Rollback: Revert to previous reconciler and enable emergency throttle if misbehaving; fall back to the mitigation dataplane guard while investigating.
Target release: runtime-2026.04; hotfix branch will contain minimal guard to be cherry-picked if expedited.
tests_and_qa: Unit tests for epoch ordering and CAS semantics on binding table updates.
Integration test harness simulating concurrent policy updates + peering flips with traffic generators.
Chaos tests: random node eviction during mutation windows to validate no cross-tenant resolution.
Load test: 10k DNS lookups/min for canary to ensure no latency regressions.
Security review: confirm serialization does not open DOS vector or allow tenant-level starvation.
monitoring_and_alerting: Add metric: resolver.binding.mismatch.count (count of checks where owner != tenant) with 1m and 5m alerts.
Add alert: spike in cross-tenant-resolution errors > 5 in 5m for production Dedicated clusters.
Dashboards: per-tenant binding epoch, reconciliation lag, SNAT-port-reuse events; include example graphs on Console.
SLO impact: create temporary burn-rate dashboard for 5xx and DNS latency during rollout window.
